articles.title: Suicide Attack On Police Facility In Northwest Pakistan Leaves Many Dead And Wounded
articles.summary: At least 16 people were reported dead and dozens were injured after an attacker drove a vehicle packed with explosives into a police complex in Pakistan. Officials said several other attackers died in a shootout with police after the blast in the city of Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province. Suicide Attack On Police Facility In Northwest Pakistan Leaves Many Dead And Wounded.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula announces higher welfare payments and free weight-loss jabs ahead of election

articles.title: Technology is transforming crime – and the response to it
articles.summary: Sitting in her Vienna office ahead of a pivotal UN gathering in Abu Dhabi, Monica Juma is focused on a simple reality: crime has evolved faster than many of the institutions designed to combat it. Technology is transforming crime – and the response to it.

articles.title: Security Council LIVE: UN peacekeeping under pressure
articles.summary: UN peacekeepers have increasingly been sent into places where there is no peace to keep – under resourced, outgunned and exposed to violence they are not equipped to counter. The Security Council meets this afternoon in New York to confront that problem, with Secretary-General António Guterres briefing ambassadors on how to close the gap. articles.title: Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak

Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak.

articles.title: Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence
articles.summary: Haiti is facing a worsening child malnutrition crisis, with an estimated 253,725 children aged 6 to 59 months projected to suffer from acute malnutrition between June 2026 and May 2027, new UN-backed analysis has revealed. Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence.

articles.title: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon

articles.title: ‘China Shock 2.0’ fuels EU push for united response to Beijing
articles.summary: Beijing has called for communication and pragmatism after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen warned of a second “China Shock” that’s damaging key manufacturing industries in the bloc. The term “China shock” originally described the wave of cheap toys, textiles and basic electronics that flooded European markets after China joined the World Trade Organization [] The post ‘China Sho.

articles.title: US Senator Jeanne Shaheen: 'Putin Is Trying To Wait Us Out'
articles.summary: With a sweeping Russia sanctions bill headed to President Donald Trump’s desk, US Senator Jeanne Shaheen tells RFE/RL the legislation is intended to squeeze Moscow’s energy revenues and pressure countries buying Russian oil and gas. US Senator Jeanne Shaheen: 'Putin Is Trying To Wait Us Out'.

articles.title: A Pivotal Moment in Uniting Post-Assad Syria
articles.summary: The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, which long enjoyed de facto autonomy in north-eastern Syria, have dissolved. But tensions in the region remain high as talks about integration with the central state proceed. Further compromise would set a useful precedent for other parts of the country. A Pivotal Moment in Uniting Post-Assad Syria.

articles.title: UN fact-finding mission on Iran focuses on plight of civilians
articles.summary: The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran confirmed that civilians in the country suffered serious human rights violations and “crimes against humanity committed by their government,” while finding "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed “war crimes” in the context of its ongoing conflict with the Islamic Republic. UN fact-finding mission on Iran focuses on plight of civilians.

articles.title: Will the Houthis Shut Down the Bab al-Mandab Strait?
articles.summary: In this special episode of Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group expert Ahmed Nagi about the rapid Houthi advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, what they mean for Saudi Arabia and the wider region, and the risk of a broader shipping crisis. Will the Houthis Shut Down the Bab al-Mandab Strait?

articles.title: Ten Challenges for the UN in 2026-2027
articles.summary: As the 2026 General Assembly begins, the UN remains hobbled by cost cutting and big-power wrangling. articles.title: Nuclear Deterrence in Europe (and another round of U.S. Ukraine-Russia diplomacy)

articles.summary: कर्नाटक के मुख्यमंत्री डीके शिवकुमार ने शुक्रवार को घोषणा की कि राज्य के दक्षिण कन्नड़ और उडुपी जिलों में बोली जाने वाली तुलु भाषा को उस क्षेत्र में एक अतिरिक्त प्रशासनिक भाषा के तौर पर मान्यता दी जाएगी. मंगलुरु में कैबिनेट बैठक के बाद पत्रकारों से बात करते हुए शिवकुमार ने कहा, "आज हमने उडुपी और दक्षिण कन्नड़ जिलों में तुलु भाषा को लागू करने और इसे राज्य की दूसरी अतिरिक्त प्रशासनिक भाषा घोषित करने।
